## 📄 Revised spec — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

I folded in everything you described and reversed the two earlier assumptions that conflicted with it. Here's what changed and what's now covered, as prioritized user stories:

| Priority | Story | Now includes |
|----------|-------|--------------|
| **P1** | Save a link with auto-details | Auto-fetch **title, description, favicon, preview image**; edit title/description; **duplicate → open existing bookmark, no duplicate** |
| **P1** | Browse & open | Normal list shows **title, description, tags, favicon**; open in new tab |
| **P2** | Organize | **Note**, multiple **tags** (with suggestions from tags you already use), **unread/read-later**, **archive**; separate **unread** and **archived** views; archived hidden from normal browsing/search |
| **P2** | Search precisely | Case-insensitive across **title/description/note/address**; **`#tag`**, **exact phrases**, **AND/OR/NOT + parentheses**; **sorting** |
| **P3** | Bulk actions | Multi-select bulk changes **and** "apply to everything matching the current view" |
| **P3** | Saved searches | Name, reopen, rename, delete a query+filters+sort |
| **P3** | Snapshots & Internet Archive | Local page snapshot (**PDF kept as PDF**); submit to **Internet Archive** and record the link |
| **P3** | Import/export | **Netscape bookmark-file** import and export |
| **P3** | Display preferences | Default **sort**, **items shown**, **font size**; persisted |

Backed by **34 functional requirements** (FR-001–034), an expanded **Key Entities** set (Bookmark, Tag, Saved Search, Snapshot, Display Preferences), edge cases (partial/slow metadata, PDF targets, invalid boolean expressions, Internet Archive unavailable, low local storage), and measurable success criteria including "duplicate opens existing in 100% of cases," "archived appears in 0% of normal results," and "exported Netscape file re-imports into a mainstream browser."

### A few notes for your review

- **Assumptions updated:** automatic metadata capture and browser import/export are now marked **in scope** (previously excluded). Single-user browser app, same-device storage, and http/https-only remain as you confirmed.
- **Snapshots/Internet Archive** depend on the target page and the archive service being reachable — the spec treats failures as recoverable rather than blocking the bookmark.
- I kept it technology-agnostic (no framework/storage decisions) — those belong in the plan.

### 👉 At this gate

- **Approve** and I'll proceed to `speckit-plan` (still no code until you approve the plan too).
- **Want changes** to scope, priorities, or any requirement? Tell me and I'll revise.
- **Want structured clarifying questions first?** I can run `speckit-clarify`.

I'll wait for your go-ahead.
